title: Congress Failed to Extend the Health Care Subsidies. Now What?

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是 Benjamin Poulin，我是 Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着 300 件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《The Reframers》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的 Rachel Abrams，这是《The Daily》节目。

sentences.en: I don't really pray much, but I pray at night that something happens, that I wake up in the morning and I check the news and that the subsidy was extended.
sentences.zh: 我其实不太常祈祷，但我每天晚上都会祈祷能发生点什么，祈祷我早上醒来查看新闻时，发现补贴已经延长了。

sentences.en: Something that will make it not $55,000 next year, something.
sentences.zh: 哪怕是什么能让明年的费用不至于涨到 55,000 美元的东西都行。

sentences.en: This week, despite a last-ditch effort by some House Republicans to strike a deal on health care,
sentences.zh: 本周，尽管一些众议院共和党人试图在医疗保健问题上达成协议，但最终还是做了最后的努力，

sentences.en: Capitol Hill remains deadlocked on whether to extend support for millions of Americans who get their health care through the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 国会山在是否要继续支持数百万通过《平价医疗法案》获得医保的美国人这一问题上，依然陷入僵局。

sentences.en: Without the subsidies, it would be the minimum of $1,500 a month and there wasn't no way.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这些补贴，每个月至少要交 1,500 美元，这根本没法负担。

sentences.en: My original estimate was about a 1,200 percent increase.
sentences.zh: 我最初的估算涨幅大约是 1,200%。

sentences.en: I think I was in tears the entire rest of the week after I got that news.
sentences.zh: 得到那个消息后，我想我那一整周都在流泪。

sentences.en: That's left those Americans to confront a wrenching decision.
sentences.zh: 这让那些美国人不得不面对一个痛苦的抉择。

sentences.en: I asked my husband, like, what should we do?
sentences.zh: 我问我丈夫，我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: He's like, maybe we go without health insurance.
sentences.zh: 他说，也许我们只能不买医疗保险了。

sentences.en: And I was like, oh my God, no way.
sentences.zh: 我说，天哪，绝对不行。

sentences.en: Keep paying for rising insurance costs or risk going without it.
sentences.zh: 要么继续支付不断上涨的保险费，要么冒着没有保险的风险。

sentences.en: It's been a really tough couple of months.
sentences.zh: 这几个月真的太难熬了。

sentences.en: A lot of just, like, mentally preparing for what this next year is going to look like.
sentences.zh: 大部分时间都在做心理准备，去面对接下来的一年将会是什么样子。

sentences.en: And it's pretty grim.
sentences.zh: 而且前景相当严峻。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Margo Sanger-Katz explains who will be most affected and how this could all change the political landscape heading into the midterMs.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事 Margo Sanger-Katz 将解释谁受到的影响最大，以及这一切将如何改变中期选举前的政治格局。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, December 18th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 12 月 18 日，星期四。

sentences.en: Margo, welcome back to The Daily.
sentences.zh: Margo，欢迎回到《The Daily》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: It really feels like health care and debates over health insurance have been in the news, like, every other day almoSt.
sentences.zh: 感觉医疗保健和医保相关的辩论几乎每隔一天就会出现在新闻里。

sentences.en: And in large part, that's because there have been these really huge and ongoing and changing debates on Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 在很大程度上，这是因为国会山一直在进行着激烈、持续且不断变化的辩论。

sentences.en: But it really feels like this week in particular, we have reached an inflection point, which is why we wanted to have you on the show.
sentences.zh: 但感觉特别是在本周，我们已经到了一个转折点，这就是为什么我们想请你来参加节目。

sentences.en: The last time we had you on, it was in the thick of the shutdown fight.
sentences.zh: 上次你来的时候，正值政府停摆之争最激烈的时候。

sentences.en: And we're bringing you back here so that you can bring us up to speed on where we are now.
sentences.zh: 我们再次邀请你，是为了让你帮我们梳理一下目前的进展。

sentences.en: So, as you may remember,
sentences.zh: 那么，你可能还记得，

sentences.en: the real crux of the fight over the shutdown was whether or not Congress was going to extend these subsidies that help people buy insurance in the Affordable Care Act marketplaces.
sentences.zh: 政府停摆之争的核心在于国会是否会延长那些帮助人们在《平价医疗法案》市场购买保险的补贴。

sentences.en: This was the thing that Democrats decided to make the centerpiece of their fight.
sentences.zh: 民主党人决定将此作为他们斗争的核心议题。

sentences.en: And they chose to fight over these subsidies specifically because I think they felt like this was a really strong issue for them.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以选择专门针对这些补贴进行抗争，是因为我认为他们觉得这是一个对他们非常有利的议题。

sentences.en: Voters trust them more on health care.
sentences.zh: 选民在医疗保健问题上更信任他们。

sentences.en: It's like one of the Democrats' strongest issues, but it has not been the biggest issue that was in the forefront of people's mind.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是民主党最强有力的议题之一，但它并不是人们心目中最首要的问题。

sentences.en: It was a little bit of a gamble.
sentences.zh: 这多少有点赌博的意味。

sentences.en: You know, were they going to be able to get people to pay attention to this?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们能让人们关注这件事吗？

sentences.en: But they did.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实做到了。

sentences.en: And it didn't work from the perspective of getting legislation passed.
sentences.zh: 不过从通过立法的角度来看，这并没有奏效。

sentences.en: They shut down the government for a record period of time.
sentences.zh: 他们让政府停摆了创纪录的时间。

sentences.en: Ultimately, they decided to reopen the government without legislation to extend these subsidies.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们决定在没有延长补贴立法的情况下重启政府。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Democrats basically lost that fight.
sentences.zh: 民主党基本上输掉了那场斗争。

sentences.en: They agreed to reopen the government with no deal on these health care subsidies.
sentences.zh: 他们同意在没有达成医保补贴协议的情况下重启政府。

sentences.en: The one deal they got is that they were going to get to put up a vote on the Senate floor.
sentences.zh: 他们得到的唯一协议是可以在参议院进行一次投票。

sentences.en: They did that.
sentences.zh: 他们确实那样做了。

sentences.en: Republicans didn't vote for it.
sentences.zh: 但共和党人没有投赞成票。

sentences.en: It didn't go anywhere.
sentences.zh: 投票结果不了了之。

sentences.en: So that was all they got was a kind of failed vote on this issue.
sentences.zh: 所以他们得到的仅仅是一次关于该议题的失败投票。

sentences.en: And then since then, a lot of Republican lawmakers, particularly moderate Republicans in the House,
sentences.zh: 从那以后，许多共和党议员，特别是众议院的温和派共和党人，

sentences.en: have been worried about what to do because they know that the loss of these subsidies is going to affect their constituents.
sentences.zh: 一直很担心该怎么办，因为他们知道补贴的取消会影响到他们的选民。

sentences.en: And I think they're worried about political consequences when the midterms roll around.
sentences.zh: 我想他们很担心中期选举到来时会产生政治后果。

sentences.en: So there's been this kind of deal-making debate between some of these moderate Republicans and Democrats.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些温和派共和党人和民主党人之间一直存在着某种关于达成协议的辩论。

sentences.en: Could they form a compromise?
sentences.zh: 他们能达成妥协吗？

sentences.en: Could they pass something that would patch the subsidies and that other Republicans could sign on to?
sentences.zh: 他们能通过某种方案来修补补贴，并让其他共和党人也加入进来吗？

sentences.en: But the deadline for enrollment came on Monday and they did not pass anything like that.
sentences.zh: 但注册截止日期是周一，他们并没有通过任何类似的方案。

sentences.en: So this is the open enrollment that we're all quite familiar with at this point from the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们现在对《平价医疗法案》非常熟悉的公开注册期。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, you probably have the same thing for like we have the same thing here at the Times for our work insurance.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可能也有同样的经历，我们《时报》内部的工作保险也是这样。

sentences.en: There's some period of time in which you have to pick and pay for your health insurance and that signs you up for the whole year.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间你需要选择并支付医疗保险，一旦选定，就涵盖全年。

sentences.en: And there are just our deadlines that happen every year.
sentences.zh: 每年都有这样的截止日期。

sentences.en: So even though we're not at the end of the year now, we're kind of a little bit at the end of the line for these subsidies.
sentences.zh: 所以即使现在不是年底，但对于这些补贴来说，我们已经到了最后关头。

sentences.en: People had to make their choices.
sentences.zh: 人们必须做出选择。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, that said, it may not be totally over.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，这可能还没完全结束。

sentences.en: This week, something kind of unusual happened.
sentences.zh: 本周发生了一件不同寻常的事情。

sentences.en: A couple of moderate Republicans who are really mad at the Speaker of the House for not giving them a chance to vote on this joined up with all of the Democrats to sign what's called a discharge petition,
sentences.zh: 几位对众议院议长不给他们投票机会感到非常愤怒的温和派共和党人，联合所有民主党人签署了一份所谓的“解除请愿书”（discharge petition），

sentences.en: which is a way to get a bill on the floor without the House Speaker's cooperation.
sentences.zh: 这是一种在没有众议院议长配合的情况下将法案提交表决的方法。

sentences.en: And that bill would extend the subsidies for three years.
sentences.zh: 该法案将把补贴延长三年。

sentences.en: But that bill isn't going to come up for a vote for probably a couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 但该法案可能还要几周时间才能进行投票。

sentences.en: And it's not clear whether it can pass the Senate.
sentences.zh: 而且它能否在参议院通过还不清楚。

sentences.en: So for now, it looks like these subsidies are going to expire and a lot of people are going to have to pay more for their health insurance.
sentences.zh: 所以目前看来，这些补贴即将到期，很多人将不得不支付更多的医疗保险费用。

sentences.en: So the key word that we have been using a lot here is subsidies.
sentences.zh: 我们一直提到的关键词是“补贴”。

sentences.en: But I want to make sure that people actually understand what that means.
sentences.zh: 但我希望能确保大家真正理解它的含义。

sentences.en: Specifically, what were the subsidies and how are they changing?
sentences.zh: 具体来说，这些补贴是什么，它们又是如何变化的？

sentences.en: So if you will indulge me, I think it makes sense to go back in time a little bit and talk about Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 如果你不介意的话，我觉得有必要回顾一下过去，谈谈“奥巴马医改”。

sentences.en: So when Democrats passed the Affordable Care Act in 2010, they set up a system where people who don't get their insurance through work or through a government program
sentences.zh: 2010 年民主党通过《平价医疗法案》时，他们建立了一个系统，让那些无法通过工作或政府项目获得保险的人

sentences.en: have access to a market.
sentences.zh: 能够进入一个市场。

sentences.en: And if they make less than 400 percent of the federal poverty level, that's like $63,000 this year.
sentences.zh: 如果他们的收入低于联邦贫困线的 400%，也就是今年大约 63,000 美元，

sentences.en: Might sound like a lot, 400 percent, but that is...
sentences.zh: 400% 听起来可能很多，但那是……

sentences.en: For a single person, it's like $63,000.
sentences.zh: 对于单身人士来说，大约是 63,000 美元。

sentences.en: For a larger family, you might be talking about $100,000.
sentences.zh: 对于大家庭，可能就是 100,000 美元左右。

sentences.en: If you make less than that, you get some help buying your insurance.
sentences.zh: 如果你的收入低于这个标准，你就能获得一些购买保险的补助。

sentences.en: And it's on a sort of sliding scale.
sentences.zh: 而且它是按某种浮动比例计算的。

sentences.en: So the poorer you are, the more help you get.
sentences.zh: 所以你越穷，得到的帮助就越多。

sentences.en: And the idea was to make insurance affordable for people who didn't have it.
sentences.zh: 其初衷是让那些没有保险的人也能负担得起保险。

sentences.en: But over time, what a lot of the authors of the Affordable Care Act realized is that the health insurance was still kind of expensive for these people who are uninsured.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，《平价医疗法案》的许多起草者意识到，对于这些没有保险的人来说，医疗保险仍然有些昂贵。

sentences.en: So going into the pandemic, there were around 12 million people who were signed up for Obamacare plans.
sentences.zh: 因此在疫情爆发前，大约有 1200 万人注册了奥巴马医改计划。

sentences.en: That was less than everyone had expected when the bill passed.
sentences.zh: 这比法案通过时所有人的预期都要少。

sentences.en: And so when the pandemic happened and there was this real openness to spending more money by the federal government, Democrats revisited those original subsidies
sentences.zh: 所以当疫情发生，联邦政府表现出真正愿意增加支出时，民主党人重新审视了那些最初的补贴，

sentences.en: and they topped them off with new subsidies that made the payments even more generous and asked people to pay even less of the total bill for their health coverage.
sentences.zh: 并用新的补贴对它们进行了补充，使支付额度更加慷慨，并要求人们在医疗保险总费用中承担更少的比例。

sentences.en: So what did those more generous subsidies look like?
sentences.zh: 那么这些更慷慨的补贴是什么样的呢？

sentences.en: So under the system that Democrats passed during the pandemic, basically everyone who buys insurance in this market got more financial help.
sentences.zh: 在民主党疫情期间通过的系统下，基本上在这个市场购买保险的每个人都获得了更多的经济援助。

sentences.en: But there are two groups that I think benefited particularly.
sentences.zh: 但我认为有两个群体受益尤为明显。

sentences.en: One group was the poorest Americans in this market.
sentences.zh: 一个是该市场中最贫困的美国人群体。

sentences.en: The way the Affordable Care Act calculates that is anyone who earns less than one and a half times the federal poverty level in a given year.
sentences.zh: 《平价医疗法案》的计算方式是，任何一年收入低于联邦贫困线 1.5 倍的人。

sentences.en: That's a little less than $25,000 this year.
sentences.zh: 今年这大约不到 25,000 美元。

sentences.en: The Democrats reset the subsidies so that those people have to pay nothing.
sentences.zh: 民主党人重新设定了补贴，使这些人无需支付任何费用。

sentences.en: Nothing.
sentences.zh: 什么都不用付。

sentences.en: Zero.
sentences.zh: 零。

sentences.en: They can get an insurance plan basically for free.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上可以免费获得一份保险计划。

sentences.en: And then there's a new group who actually didn't get any subsidies under the original Obamacare design
sentences.zh: 还有一个新的群体，他们在最初的奥巴马医改设计下实际上没有得到任何补贴，

sentences.en: who were now under this enhanced subsidy structure getting help for the first time.
sentences.zh: 现在在这一增强的补贴结构下首次获得了帮助。

sentences.en: So these are people who earn more than 400 percent of the federal poverty level.
sentences.zh: 这些人收入超过了联邦贫困线的 400%。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is a group that includes a lot of entrepreneurs, people who work for small businesses that can't offer insurance,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这个群体包括许多创业者、在无法提供保险的小企业工作的人、

sentences.en: farmers and ranchers, and also early retirees who either chose to stop working early before they qualified for Medicare or maybe lost their job
sentences.zh: 农民和牧场主，以及那些在获得联邦医疗保险（Medicare）资格前选择提前退休，或者可能失业了，

sentences.en: and were having trouble getting back into the job market and are living off their savings.
sentences.zh: 在重返就业市场时遇到困难，只能靠积蓄生活的人。

sentences.en: So basically it sounds like the Democrats decided that not only did the subsidies need to get more generous, but they also needed to be available to a lot more people.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上听起来，民主党人认为不仅补贴需要更慷慨，而且还需要让更多人能够享受到。

sentences.en: Well, I think this was a group that a lot of Democrats felt were really slipping between the cracks.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这是一个许多民主党人觉得真正被遗漏的群体。

sentences.en: And so I think Democrats were kind of happy to come back and try to fix this program.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为民主党人很高兴能回来尝试修复这个项目。

sentences.en: And it actually made a very big financial difference for some of these people.
sentences.zh: 这对其中一些人来说确实产生了巨大的经济影响。

sentences.en: So that's the plan that Democrats implemented in 2021.
sentences.zh: 这就是民主党在 2021 年实施的计划。

sentences.en: And at first they made it really short term.
sentences.zh: 起初他们将其设定为短期方案。

sentences.en: But then they immediately saw that tons more people were signing up for coverage.
sentences.zh: 但随后他们立即发现有大量的人注册了保险。

sentences.en: Do we know who was really driving that surge?
sentences.zh: 我们知道是谁在真正推动这种激增吗？

sentences.en: What kind of people?
sentences.zh: 是什么样的人？

sentences.en: What kind of income level?
sentences.zh: 什么样的收入水平？

sentences.en: From that bottom income category.
sentences.zh: 来自最低收入类别的那部分人。

sentences.en: So those are the people that are eligible for these zero dollar premiuMs.
sentences.zh: 所以他们就是那些有资格获得零美元保费的人。

sentences.en: I think there are a couple of reasons why that happened.
sentences.zh: 我认为发生这种情况有几个原因。

sentences.en: One is just that's a group that's much more likely to be uninsured.
sentences.zh: 一是这一群体本身就更容易没有保险。

sentences.en: If you think about the kinds of jobs that low income people have, they're just much less likely to come with health insurance.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想低收入人群从事的工作类型，它们通常不太可能提供医疗保险。

sentences.en: You know, if there's someone who has a bunch of gig economy jobs that they're patching together
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果有人做着一堆零工经济的工作来维持生计，

sentences.en: or a part-time job, those are the kinds of jobs generally don't have health insurance.
sentences.zh: 或者做兼职工作，这些工作通常都没有医疗保险。

sentences.en: And so those people are really benefiting from the ability to go get a free plan somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人确实从能够去别处获得免费计划的能力中受益匪浅。

sentences.en: It's also like free is a really important horizon, it turns out.
sentences.zh: 而且事实证明，“免费”是一个非常重要的门槛。

sentences.en: Even asking people to pay a small amount can really discourage them, and particularly low income people from enrolling in these kind of prograMs.
sentences.zh: 即使要求人们支付少量费用，也确实会阻碍他们，特别是低收入人群注册这类项目。

sentences.en: A lot of really low income people don't even have a bank account.
sentences.zh: 很多极低收入的人甚至连银行账户都没有。

sentences.en: And so if you just imagine the mechanics of like, how is that person going to pay a monthly premium?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想象一下，那个人该如何支付月保费的运作方式？

sentences.en: They can't write a check.
sentences.zh: 他们没法开支票。

sentences.en: They don't have a credit card.
sentences.zh: 他们没有信用卡。

sentences.en: Not impossible, but it makes it harder.
sentences.zh: 这并非不可能，但确实增加了难度。

sentences.en: What did Republicans think of all these changes to the Obamacare subsidies?
sentences.zh: 共和党人对奥巴马医改补贴的这些变化有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's important to remember Republicans never liked Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为重要的是要记住，共和党人从来都不喜欢奥巴马医改。

sentences.en: They felt like it was a waste of money.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得这是在浪费钱。

sentences.en: They thought it was putting too many rules on the health insurance system.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这给医疗保险系统施加了太多的规则。

sentences.en: And this was a huge expansion.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一次巨大的扩张。

sentences.en: It's a lot more dollars.
sentences.zh: 涉及的资金多得多。

sentences.en: It was bringing more people into the system.
sentences.zh: 它将更多的人纳入了系统。

sentences.en: And I think they also objected to some of the specific policy changes.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他们也反对其中一些具体的政策变化。

sentences.en: They really didn't like the idea that all these people were going to get insurance for free.
sentences.zh: 他们真的不喜欢这些人都能免费获得保险的想法。

sentences.en: It felt sort of unfair to them.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说似乎有点不公平。

sentences.en: Everyone else has to pay something for health insurance.
sentences.zh: 其他人买医疗保险都得付钱。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of Republican lawmakers feel like even these very low income people, if they really value their insurance, they should have to pay some minimal amount
sentences.zh: 而且我认为许多共和党议员觉得，即使是这些极低收入的人，如果他们真的重视自己的保险，也应该支付一些最低限度的费用，

sentences.en: just to prove that it's something that they really want and need.
sentences.zh: 以此证明这是他们真正想要和需要的东西。

sentences.en: But of course, that didn't matter at the time because the Democrats controlled the entire government.
sentences.zh: 但当然，当时这并不重要，因为民主党控制了整个政府。

sentences.en: They had the Senate, the House, and the White House.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有参议院、众议院和白宫。

sentences.en: So when 2022 rolled around, the Democrats decided to extend these more generous subsidies for even longer.
sentences.zh: 所以当 2022 年到来时，民主党决定将这些更慷慨的补贴延长更长时间。

sentences.en: They just weren't able to make them permanent because, as you may remember,
sentences.zh: 他们只是无法使其永久化，因为正如你可能记得的那样，

sentences.en: Joe Manchin, the conservative Democratic senator from West Virginia, insisted that they not make this a permanent policy.
sentences.zh: 来自西弗吉尼亚州的保守派民主党参议员 Joe Manchin 坚持要求他们不要将此作为永久性政策。

sentences.en: Democrats chose to have the policy expire in 2025 because they were hoping that they would have enough
sentences.zh: 民主党人选择让该政策在2025年到期，是因为他们当时希望自己能有足够的

sentences.en: control in the government that they would be able to eke out a bipartisan compromise to extend the subsidies further.
sentences.zh: 政府控制权，从而能够勉强达成两党妥协，进一步延长这些补贴。

sentences.en: But of course, that's not what happened.
sentences.zh: 但当然，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And Republicans swept to power in 2024.
sentences.zh: 共和党人在2024年大获全胜，掌握了权力。

sentences.en: And that's why we're now in this situation where the only way that they were able to advocate for this policy was by shutting down the government.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们现在陷入了这种境地：他们唯一能为这项政策辩护的方式，就是让政府停摆。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And so that brings us to this moment where the subsidies are expiring.
sentences.zh: 这也就把我们带到了补贴即将到期的这一刻。

sentences.en: No agreement has been reached.
sentences.zh: 目前尚未达成任何协议。

sentences.en: What do we know about the people who would be most impacted by the fact that these are going away?
sentences.zh: 对于那些受补贴取消影响最大的人，我们了解多少？

sentences.en: Basically, everyone in this market is going to be affected to some degree.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这个市场里的每个人都会在一定程度上受到影响。

sentences.en: I said there were around 12 million people in the market before the extra subsidies.
sentences.zh: 我之前说过，在额外补贴出台前，市场里大约有1200万人。

sentences.en: Now, there are about 24 million people in the market.
sentences.zh: 现在，市场里大约有2400万人。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: So this low-income group we were just talking about, that's the biggest group.
sentences.zh: 所以我们刚才提到的这个低收入群体，是最大的群体。

sentences.en: It's like half the market.
sentences.zh: 几乎占了市场的一半。

sentences.en: And those people are going to have to go from paying nothing for their insurance to paying somewhere around $50 a month for their insurance.
sentences.zh: 这些人将不得不从原本无需支付保险费，转变为每月支付大约50美元的保险费。

sentences.en: Then there's this kind of middle-income group.
sentences.zh: 然后是中等收入群体。

sentences.en: And those people are also going to have to pay more for their insurance, probably somewhere in the neighborhood of like $150 more per month on average.
sentences.zh: 这些人也必须为保险支付更多费用，平均每月可能要多花150美元左右。

sentences.en: And then you get to this group earning more than $65,000.
sentences.zh: 接下来是收入超过65000美元的群体。

sentences.en: And that is a small share of the market.
sentences.zh: 这部分人在市场中占比很小。

sentences.en: But in dollar terms, those are the people that are facing the biggest effects.
sentences.zh: 但从金额上看，他们才是面临最大影响的人。

sentences.en: Some of those people are looking at price increases in the neighborhood of
sentences.zh: 其中一些人面临的价格上涨幅度在

sentences.en: $1,000 or even $2,000 more per month without these enhanced subsidies.
sentences.zh: 每月1000甚至2000美元左右，如果没有这些增强型补贴的话。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because for that group, those highest earners, their subsidies are going away entirely.
sentences.zh: 因为对于这群高收入者来说，他们的补贴将完全消失。

sentences.en: And so they'll see the biggest potential increase.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会看到最大的潜在涨幅。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: They are looking at just absolutely huge and astronomical price increases that may be impossible for some of them to pay.
sentences.zh: 他们面临的是绝对巨大且天文数字般的价格上涨，其中一些人可能根本无法负担。

sentences.en: So over the last few weeks, as people in all of these income categories have been looking at their options and thinking about the ongoing drama in Washington,
sentences.zh: 所以在过去几周里，当所有这些收入阶层的人都在审视自己的选择，并思考华盛顿正在上演的闹剧时，

sentences.en: I think a lot of them have started to consider some really difficult choices.
sentences.zh: 我想他们中的许多人已经开始考虑一些非常艰难的抉择。

sentences.en: Should they buy a less generous plan with a really high deductible so they don't have to pay as much?
sentences.zh: 他们应该购买一份保障较少、免赔额极高的保险计划，这样就不用付那么多钱了吗？

sentences.en: Should they try to rearrange their work so maybe they earn less and they get right under that threshold where they could qualify for a subsidy?
sentences.zh: 他们是否应该尝试调整工作，也许少赚点钱，刚好降到能获得补贴的门槛之下？

sentences.en: Do they need to earn more money, get a second job, or cut back on some of their living expenses in order to be able to pay the premium?
sentences.zh: 他们是否需要赚更多的钱、找第二份工作，或者削减一些生活开支，以便能够支付保费？

sentences.en: And all of that has really come to a head this week.
sentences.zh: 而这一切在本周达到了顶峰。

sentences.en: When the deadline hit, the subsidies were not extended, and people had to ultimately decide what kind of insurance they were going to choose, if any insurance at all.
sentences.zh: 当截止日期到来时，补贴没有延长，人们最终不得不决定选择什么样的保险，甚至是否还要买保险。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 致力于帮助您了解世界，并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，获取 nytimes.com/subscribe 的特别优惠。

sentences.en: Hello?
sentences.zh: 喂？

sentences.en: Good morning, this is Lizzie.
sentences.zh: 早上好，我是莉齐。

sentences.en: Hey, this is Anna from The Times.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是《纽约时报》的安娜。

sentences.en: How are you doing?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: All right, I can help you.
sentences.zh: 好的，我可以帮你。

sentences.en: Daily producer Anna Foley has been talking to people who get their insurance through the Affordable Care Act marketplace to hear more about how they're navigating the reduction
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》制片人安娜·福利一直在与通过《平价医疗法案》市场购买保险的人交谈，以了解他们如何应对

sentences.en: in subsidies.
sentences.zh: 补贴减少的问题。

sentences.en: Why don't you just go ahead and start by telling me a little bit about yourself?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不先简单介绍一下你自己呢？

sentences.en: I live in Mountain City, Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 我住在田纳西州的芒廷城。

sentences.en: I was a delivery driver for Amazon.
sentences.zh: 我曾经是亚马逊的送货司机。

sentences.en: I work for a small family business.
sentences.zh: 我现在为一家小型家族企业工作。

sentences.en: I run my daughter's tattoo shop.
sentences.zh: 我经营着我女儿的纹身店。

sentences.en: So I am a small business owner.
sentences.zh: 所以我是一名小企业主。

sentences.en: Do you like being your own boss?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢当自己的老板吗？

sentences.en: You know, it suits my personality type.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很适合我的性格。

sentences.en: I don't like people telling me what to do.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢别人对我指手画脚。

sentences.en: But honestly, the stressors of things like this, of health care, it's gotten really hairy.
sentences.zh: 但老实说，像医疗保健这类事情带来的压力，真的变得非常棘手。

sentences.en: It's gotten really, really difficult.
sentences.zh: 变得非常、非常困难。

sentences.en: There were truly no good options.
sentences.zh: 真的没有好的选择。

sentences.en: Every single plan forced me to compromise on costs, on providers, and on prescriptions.
sentences.zh: 每一个计划都迫使我在成本、医疗服务提供者和处方药上做出妥协。

sentences.en: Every single one of them.
sentences.zh: 每一个都是如此。

sentences.en: I have a rare chronic illness called eosinophilic asthma.
sentences.zh: 我患有一种罕见的慢性病，叫嗜酸性粒细胞性哮喘。

sentences.en: And I need to receive a specialty biologic injection every month in order to be able to breathe.
sentences.zh: 我每个月都需要注射一种特殊的生物制剂，才能正常呼吸。

sentences.en: And the co-pays on that drug alone are $350 a month, which takes my overall health care costs to about $700 a month.
sentences.zh: 仅这种药的自付费用就高达每月350美元，这使我的医疗总支出达到每月700美元左右。

sentences.en: It's a shame that it's a luxury to have air in my lungs.
sentences.zh: 能呼吸到空气竟然成了一种奢侈，真是可悲。

sentences.en: What are you going to have to change in your life to now cover this health care cost?
sentences.zh: 为了支付这笔医疗费用，你生活中必须做出什么改变？

sentences.en: I'm having to make wholesale decisions about my career based on my health insurance.
sentences.zh: 我不得不根据我的医疗保险来对职业生涯做出全面调整。

sentences.en: Like, after all these years and all this expertise I've built, do I go down to Starbucks and just work at Starbucks for benefits and make nothing,
sentences.zh: 比如，在积累了这么多年的经验和专业知识后，我是不是该去星巴克工作，只为了那点福利，虽然赚不到什么钱，

sentences.en: but at least I have catastrophic coverage for my family?
sentences.zh: 但至少能为我的家人提供灾难性医疗保险？

sentences.en: I already live a very frugal lifestyle, so it's just going to be that on steroids, you know.
sentences.zh: 我本来生活就很节俭，所以这只会变本加厉，你懂的。

sentences.en: More cuban-ing, walking to work instead of driving my car.
sentences.zh: 更多地步行上班，而不是开车。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: How far is that walk?
sentences.zh: 那段路有多远？

sentences.en: Three miles.
sentences.zh: 三英里。

sentences.en: Oh, that's not nothing.
sentences.zh: 哦，那可不近。

sentences.en: It isn't nothing, no.
sentences.zh: 确实不近，没错。

sentences.en: Oh, and Christmas this year has already been difficult.
sentences.zh: 哦，今年的圣诞节已经很难过了。

sentences.en: I wanted to give my mom hearing aids for Christmas, but now I've settled on a couple Yankee candles instead.
sentences.zh: 我本来想给妈妈买助听器作为圣诞礼物，但现在只能退而求其次，买了几支扬基蜡烛。

sentences.en: I also got married this year, but that changes things monetarily, right?
sentences.zh: 我今年也结婚了，但这在经济上改变了情况，对吧？

sentences.en: Because if your family household size is one, you are able to make significantly more as one person than you are as two people.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你的家庭人口规模是1人，你作为单身人士能赚的钱要比两个人一起赚得多得多。

sentences.en: You know, like, so when you get married, you can only make up to $84,600 to stay under that 400% poverty level.
sentences.zh: 你知道，结婚后，为了保持在400%贫困线以下，你们的总收入不能超过84600美元。

sentences.en: So, it's like, do we just get divorced?
sentences.zh: 所以，我们在想，我们要不要干脆离婚？

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Like, it's something we're considering is getting divorced.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们正在考虑的事情，离婚。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We're kind of stuck with no option, basically, without these subsidies.
sentences.zh: 没有这些补贴，我们基本上陷入了绝境，别无选择。

sentences.en: So, you know, thankfully we stay as healthy as we possibly can, but, you know, we're just going to have to hope for the best and just pay out of pocket as needed.
sentences.zh: 所以，谢天谢地，我们尽可能保持健康，但我们只能祈祷一切顺利，并根据需要自掏腰包。

sentences.en: So, as of right now, you don't have health insurance for 2026?
sentences.zh: 所以，截至目前，你还没有2026年的医疗保险？

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, we only have it through December 31st of this year.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们现在的保险只到今年12月31日。

sentences.en: I've had several family members to see, and they're hoping they'll get the, Congress will get their act together and get something passed to help out.
sentences.zh: 我见过几位家人，他们希望国会能采取行动，通过一些法案来提供帮助。

sentences.en: Otherwise, they're going to have to drop their insurance.
sentences.zh: 否则，他们将不得不放弃保险。

sentences.en: There are a few things out in the world that I cannot control myself.
sentences.zh: 世界上有些事情是我无法控制的。

sentences.en: I'm a total control freak.
sentences.zh: 我是一个彻头彻尾的控制狂。

sentences.en: Like, I need the government to help in very few situations.
sentences.zh: 比如，我只需要政府在极少数情况下提供帮助。

sentences.en: The rest, I promise I will take care of.
sentences.zh: 剩下的，我保证自己能处理好。

sentences.en: This is a blinding bright light where people need help.
sentences.zh: 这是一个人们急需帮助的盲点。

sentences.en: I feel like I've done everything right my whole life, and I just feel like I've just been sold a bag of shit.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我这辈子所做的一切都是对的，但现在感觉自己被骗了。

sentences.en: And now, now what am I going to do?
sentences.zh: 现在，我现在该怎么办？

sentences.en: It's like, okay, I got to really, really rethink my future.
sentences.zh: 就像是，好吧，我必须重新审视我的未来。

sentences.en: And so, it gives me a sense of loss and bewilderment and regret.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到失落、困惑和后悔。

sentences.en: Margo, our colleague Anna Foley, who's a producer here on The Daily,
sentences.zh: 玛戈，我们的同事安娜·福利，也就是《每日新闻》的制片人，

sentences.en: has been spending a lot of time talking to people who are in the middle of making these really difficult healthcare choices right now.
sentences.zh: 花了很多时间与那些正处于艰难医疗选择中的人们交谈。

sentences.en: And I wonder if you might be able to project forward for us a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否能为我们展望一下未来？

sentences.en: Like, what might this start to look like heading into next year and beyond for these people?
sentences.zh: 比如，对于这些人来说，明年及以后会是什么样子？

sentences.en: We don't really know for sure.
sentences.zh: 我们还无法确定。

sentences.en: The Congressional Budget Office, so they're the nerds that help Congress figure out what their laws are going to do.
sentences.zh: 国会预算办公室，也就是那些帮助国会分析法律影响的专家们，

sentences.en: They think that about 2 million more people will become uninsured in 2026 as a result of this policy and almost 4 million people over the course of the next decade.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，由于这项政策，2026年将有约200万人失去保险，未来十年内将有近400万人失去保险。

sentences.en: But there are other serious analysts who have estimated a much larger impact.
sentences.zh: 但也有其他严肃的分析人士估计影响会大得多。

sentences.en: Enrollment in the marketplaces has doubled since they put this policy in place in 2021.
sentences.zh: 自2021年实施该政策以来，市场注册人数翻了一番。

sentences.en: So, if you think about all of the people who newly became insured in this market, that's 12 million people.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想想所有在这个市场中新获得保险的人，那是1200万人。

sentences.en: And we're kind of snapping back to the policy from before.
sentences.zh: 而我们现在正退回到之前的政策。

sentences.en: And on the one hand, that is really disruptive for the folks who can no longer afford their healthcare or have to dramatically rethink the healthcare they can afford.
sentences.zh: 一方面，对于那些负担不起医疗费用或不得不彻底重新考虑医疗开支的人来说，这确实具有破坏性。

sentences.en: But in some ways, it also represents a reversion back to kind of a status quo.
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，这也代表了回归到某种现状。

sentences.en: And so I'm wondering how you are thinking about the world that we are about to enter.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇你是如何看待我们即将进入的世界的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think Democrats actually have been somewhat misleading in the way that they've been talking about it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为民主党人在谈论这个问题时确实有些误导。

sentences.en: They keep acting like the subsidies are going to go away.
sentences.zh: 他们一直表现得好像补贴就要消失了一样。

sentences.en: And I think that has caused some alarm among some people that all of the subsidies are going away, that people are going to all have to pay the full cost of their health insurance.
sentences.zh: 我认为这引起了一些人的恐慌，以为所有补贴都会消失，人们将不得不支付医疗保险的全额费用。

sentences.en: And that's not true.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: What we're averting back to is the original structure of Obamacare that Democrats thought really carefully about and wrote and passed in 2010.
sentences.zh: 我们正在回归的是奥巴马医改的原始结构，这是民主党人在2010年经过深思熟虑后起草并投票通过的。

sentences.en: So we do know that way more people bought insurance with this extra financial help.
sentences.zh: 我们确实知道，有更多的人在这些额外经济援助下购买了保险。

sentences.en: It definitely does make a difference in people's lives, and it does make a big difference in people's coverage.
sentences.zh: 这确实改变了人们的生活，也对人们的保险覆盖范围产生了重大影响。

sentences.en: But there is a real debate about what level of subsidization is appropriate in these markets and whether and how much people should be asked to pay for their health insurance.
sentences.zh: 但关于这些市场中适当的补贴水平，以及人们应该为医疗保险支付多少费用，确实存在真正的争论。

sentences.en: Because, in part, over the same period of time in which we've been paying all this extra money to help people buy insurance,
sentences.zh: 因为在某种程度上，在我们投入大量额外资金帮助人们购买保险的这段时间里，

sentences.en: the cost of insurance itself has gotten a lot more expensive.
sentences.zh: 保险本身的成本也变得昂贵得多。

sentences.en: And why is it that health insurance has gotten so expensive over the last few years?
sentences.zh: 为什么医疗保险在过去几年里变得如此昂贵？

sentences.en: So people love to rag on health insurance companies, and no one really likes them.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢抨击医疗保险公司，而且没人真正喜欢它们。

sentences.en: They don't like how expensive they are.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢保险费用太高。

sentences.en: There are lots of other things they don't like about them.
sentences.zh: 还有很多其他他们不喜欢的地方。

sentences.en: But the reason why health insurance is so expensive is because health care in the United States is really expensive, and the costs are growing over time.
sentences.zh: 但医疗保险之所以昂贵，是因为美国的医疗保健本身就很贵，而且成本还在不断增长。

sentences.en: And there are a bunch of reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 这背后有很多原因。

sentences.en: Recently, of course, we've had these GLP-1 anti-obesity medications, super transformative drugs.
sentences.zh: 当然，最近我们有了GLP-1抗肥胖药物，这些药物具有革命性的意义。

sentences.en: They really could help a lot of people improve their health, but they're costly, and lots of people want to take them.
sentences.zh: 它们确实可以帮助很多人改善健康，但它们成本高昂，而且很多人都想使用。

sentences.en: Another trend in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国医疗体系的另一个趋势是，

sentences.en: health care system, which is that we love to use new technology.
sentences.zh: 我们热衷于使用新技术。

sentences.en: When there are new drugs or treatments on the cutting edge that really seem to make a difference in public health, we want to use them,
sentences.zh: 当出现似乎能真正改善公共卫生的尖端药物或疗法时，我们都想使用它们，

sentences.en: even though they're going to cost a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 尽管它们会花费巨额资金。

sentences.en: I know you mentioned earlier that in the weeks since the shutdown, Republicans have been trying to get some kind of health care bill together,
sentences.zh: 我知道你之前提到，在政府停摆后的几周里，共和党人一直试图制定某种医疗保健法案，

sentences.en: and now we have this discharge petition.
sentences.zh: 现在我们有了这份请愿书。

sentences.en: But I do wonder, as of Wednesday afternoon, what appears to you like the most likely resolution to all of this?
sentences.zh: 但我确实想知道，截至周三下午，你认为最可能的解决方案是什么？

sentences.en: I think it's just really hard to say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得真的很难说。

sentences.en: We are right in the middle of this debate.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于这场辩论的中心。

sentences.en: I think what you can see with this discharge petition is that there are some Republicans who are really worried about this issue politically.
sentences.zh: 我认为从这份请愿书中可以看出，有些共和党人确实在政治上对这个问题感到担忧。

sentences.en: But you can also see that there are other Republicans who really just don't like Obamacare and don't want to be pouring more money into it,
sentences.zh: 但你也能看到，还有其他共和党人真的不喜欢奥巴马医改，不想再往里面投入更多资金，

sentences.en: and they're kind of having this fight within their own party.
sentences.zh: 他们党内似乎也存在这种分歧。

sentences.en: They control the government, and the Democrats cannot get this policy done by themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们控制着政府，而民主党人无法独自完成这项政策。

sentences.en: And so I think we're just going to have to watch over the next few weeks to see if there's some kind of compromise.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们只能在接下来的几周里拭目以待，看看是否能达成某种妥协。

sentences.en: But even if one of these bills comes together in the next few weeks or months,
sentences.zh: 但即使其中一项法案在未来几周或几个月内达成，

sentences.en: it's still going to be kind of complicated because a lot of people have already picked their plans for the year,
sentences.zh: 情况仍然会很复杂，因为很多人已经选好了今年的计划，

sentences.en: and they wouldn't have chosen their insurance knowing that these subsidies are coming back.
sentences.zh: 如果他们知道补贴会回来，他们当初就不会选择现在的保险了。

sentences.en: But I think the most likely scenario is we're kind of just snapping back to this pre-pandemic policy where people do have help buying their insurance,
sentences.zh: 但我认为最可能的情况是，我们只是回到了疫情前的政策，人们确实能获得购买保险的补助，

sentences.en: but not nearly as much as they've had in these last few years.
sentences.zh: 但远没有过去几年那么多。

sentences.en: I wonder how we should think about the political pressure that you mentioned, because not only are we heading into a midterm election year,
sentences.zh: 我想知道我们该如何看待你提到的政治压力，因为我们不仅要进入中期选举年，

sentences.en: but it was only last year that the head of UnitedHealthcare was shot and killed in the streets.
sentences.zh: 而且就在去年，联合健康集团（UnitedHealthcare）的负责人还在街头被枪杀。

sentences.en: And people were, quite frankly, cheering.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，当时人们还在欢呼。

sentences.en: They were saying that this is what happens when United and all these other insurance companies charge too much.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这就是联合健康和其他保险公司收费过高应得的下场。

sentences.en: They're taking advantage of people.
sentences.zh: 他们是在利用民众。

sentences.en: So in terms of the political implications of potentially knocking millions of people off of their health insurance, how does that change the political landscape?
sentences.zh: 那么，从可能导致数百万人失去医疗保险的政治影响来看，这会如何改变政治格局？

sentences.en: A lot of these people who have benefited from these enhanced subsidies actually don't live in the places that Democrats govern.
sentences.zh: 很多从这些增强补贴中受益的人，实际上并不住在民主党执政的地区。

sentences.en: They live in states that are controlled by Republicans and that voted for Trump in the last election.
sentences.zh: 他们住在由共和党控制、且在上届选举中投票给特朗普的州。

sentences.en: So the biggest increases of enrollment in Obamacare have been in southern states, Texas, Florida, Tennessee, Georgia.
sentences.zh: 因此，奥巴马医改（Obamacare）参保人数增长最快的地方是南部各州，如德克萨斯州、佛罗里达州、田纳西州和佐治亚州。

sentences.en: These are real Republican states,
sentences.zh: 这些可是地地道道的共和党州，

sentences.en: and those voters may have something to say if they blame their Republican lawmaker for losing this really important financial assistance that they were getting,
sentences.zh: 如果这些选民因为失去了原本获得的这项重要经济援助而责怪他们的共和党议员，他们可能会有所表示，

sentences.en: and they might vote them out of office.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能在选举中把他们投下去。

sentences.en: But I do think it's important to note this is a relatively small share of the public.
sentences.zh: 但我认为必须指出的是，这在公众中所占的比例相对较小。

sentences.en: We are only talking about 24 million people who are in this market.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论的只是这个市场中的2400万人。

sentences.en: And in overall polling, very few Americans are currently ranking health care as one of their number one issues going into the next election.
sentences.zh: 而且在整体民调中，目前很少有美国人将医疗保健列为下届选举的首要议题。

sentences.en: So I think the question is,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为问题在于，

sentences.en: does the subsidy issue start to function more like a metaphor where it's reminding Americans of their frustrations with the high cost of the health care system outside of this small market?
sentences.zh: 补贴问题是否开始演变成一种隐喻，提醒美国人关注他们在这个小市场之外，对高昂医疗成本的挫败感？

sentences.en: Because health care is getting more expensive for everyone.
sentences.zh: 因为医疗保健对每个人来说都变得越来越贵了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And of course, there's a much larger conversation happening in this country right now about affordability writ large, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，目前全国范围内正在进行一场关于整体负担能力的更大规模讨论，对吧？

sentences.en: Like even beyond health care, that is on people's minds.
sentences.zh: 就像除了医疗保健之外，这也是人们关心的问题。

sentences.en: It's certainly on voters' minds.
sentences.zh: 这无疑是选民们关心的问题。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And I think there's a real question about how this issue evolves over the course of the midterm election as Americans hear more and more stories like this from their neighbors and their family members and their friends.
sentences.zh: 我认为，随着美国人从邻居、家人和朋友那里听到越来越多这样的故事，这个问题在中期选举过程中会如何演变，确实是一个值得关注的问题。

sentences.en: Margot Sanger-Katz, thank you so much for joining us.
sentences.zh: 玛戈·桑格-卡茨（Margot Sanger-Katz），非常感谢你加入我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me on.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘（Wynna Liu）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》游戏版块谜题之一《Connections》的作者。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基（Sam Mazursky），我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”（promesthesia）的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的人们制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 请访问 nytimes.com/games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Dan Bongino, the number two official at the FBI, said on Wednesday that he would step down next month, bringing an end to his brief but tumultuous stint at the Bureau,
sentences.zh: 联邦调查局（FBI）二号人物丹·邦吉诺（Dan Bongino）周三表示，他将于下月离职，结束他在该局短暂但动荡的任期，

sentences.en: where he was known for his volcanic temper, missteps, and hyperactive presence on social media.
sentences.zh: 他以脾气火爆、行事失误以及在社交媒体上过度活跃而闻名。

sentences.en: The upheaval comes at a precarious moment for the Bureau and for the White House.
sentences.zh: 这次人事变动发生在该局和白宫都处于微妙时刻之际。

sentences.en: President Trump and his appointees, see the FBI, which long operated independently of White House interference, is a critical part of his retribution agenda.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统及其任命的官员认为，长期独立于白宫干预之外的联邦调查局，是他报复议程中的关键一环。

sentences.en: And Warner Brothers Discovery went on the attack on Wednesday against the attempted hostile takeover of the company by Paramount.
sentences.zh: 周三，华纳兄弟探索公司（Warner Brothers Discovery）对派拉蒙（Paramount）试图进行的恶意收购发起了反击。

sentences.en: Warner Brothers Discovery urged its shareholders to reject Paramount's offer, and said that Paramount's owners, the billionaire father-son duo Larry and David Ellison, have, quote,
sentences.zh: 华纳兄弟探索公司敦促其股东拒绝派拉蒙的提议，并称派拉蒙的所有者，亿万富翁父子拉里·埃里森（Larry Ellison）和大卫·埃里森（David Ellison），引用原话，

sentences.en: consistently misled them.
sentences.zh: 一直误导他们。

sentences.en: The Ellisons are determined to outmaneuver Netflix, which reached a deal to buy a large portion of Warner Brothers' business earlier this month.
sentences.zh: 埃里森父子决心胜过奈飞（Netflix），后者在本月初达成了一项收购华纳兄弟大部分业务的协议。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Anna Foley, Olivia Natt, Stella Tan, and Diana Nguyen, with reporting from Anna Foley.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由安娜·福利（Anna Foley）、奥利维亚·纳特（Olivia Natt）、斯特拉·谭（Stella Tan）和戴安娜·阮（Diana Nguyen）制作，安娜·福利负责报道。

sentences.en: It was edited by Rob Zipko.
sentences.zh: 由罗伯·齐普科（Rob Zipko）剪辑。

sentences.en: It contains music by Diane Wong, Alicia Baichu, Marion Lozano, and Pat McCusker.
sentences.zh: 节目音乐由黛安·王（Diane Wong）、艾丽西亚·拜楚（Alicia Baichu）、马里昂·洛扎诺（Marion Lozano）和帕特·麦卡斯克（Pat McCusker）创作。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 由艾丽莎·莫克斯利（Alyssa Moxley）进行工程制作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《The Daily》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs. See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我是瑞秋·艾布拉姆斯（Rachel Abrams）。明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter Show》节目，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们是否有过敏或食物敏感？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《The Wirecutter Show》。
